r_cutlass: The edge of this cutlass has been honed far more carefully than its battered hilt suggests. A smuggler may neglect his manners, but seldom the tool on which his livelihood depends.
r_ember_hatchet: Soot has settled deep into the grain of this miller's hatchet. Even after a night in cold ashes, the iron retains a little of the hearth's warmth.
r_watch_cudgel: The dents in this heavy cudgel suggest long service on the streets of Ferdok. Its former owner preferred to settle arguments before drawing a sword.
r_soft_boots: Soft felt has been stitched beneath the worn leather soles. They reward a careful step, though no cobbler can make a careless thief silent.
r_balanced_knives: These throwing knives balance neatly across a finger. The maker stamped a tiny fox beside each grip, whether from piety or a good understanding of his customers.
a_ember_saber: Fine reddish lines run beneath the surface of this Tulamide blade. When the steel grows warm, they resemble the last embers beneath a layer of ash.
a_kosch_ember_axe: A forge blessing has been hammered into the collar of this Kosch skraja. The copper inlay stays warm long after the iron around it has cooled.
a_felling_xbow: The reinforced stock and heavy steel bow were built to deliver a punishing shot. Old dents around the winding mechanism suggest that its owners valued force above elegance.
a_ogre_feller: The head of this heavy weapon bears the marks of repeated repairs. Its name was scratched into the haft by someone with considerably more confidence than penmanship.
a_viper_fang: A narrow channel runs along this blade beneath a pattern of scales. The metal carries a bitter smell that neither oil nor careful cleaning will remove.
a_tide_trident: The prongs are stained with salt, though this trident was found far from the sea. A small shell worked into the binding suggests a former owner who trusted in Efferd.
a_rondra_ward: A lion has been painted onto the leather facing and carefully renewed over older layers of colour. The battered rim speaks of a bearer more willing to stand than retreat.
a_lionheart_helm: The wings of this helm have been straightened more than once. Beneath its brow, a worn prayer asks Rondra for courage rather than an easy victory.
a_astral_robe: Silver stitches trace a measured pattern across the dark cloth. A patient observer can follow each line back to its beginning without finding a single loose end.
a_summoner_torc: Small creatures are engraved among the twists of this heavy torc. The metal gives a faint answering hum when its wearer begins an invocation.
s_rondra_reprimand: Repeated sharpening has left a narrow bright edge beneath the saber's dark spine. Its former bearer kept a prayer to Rondra wrapped inside the grip, where only a swordsmith would find it.
s_coalheart: A sliver of coal rests behind the head of this carefully forged skraja. Its copper channels remain warm even in rain; dwarven smiths disagree whether this is a blessing or merely excellent workmanship.
s_mountain_patience: Heavy iron bands bind a head of close-grained wood, each repair fitted as carefully as the first. Its dwarven maker favoured an old saying: a mountain need not hurry to have the last word.
s_nightsong: The dark wood is inlaid with silver leaves so thin that they seem to have grown beneath the surface. Travellers speak of a faint song from the string when the forest has fallen quiet.
s_heartseeker: Horn tips and sinew bindings give this Thorwalian war bow its stubborn strength. A small heart is worked into the grip: a promise from its first owner, perhaps, rather than a boast about his aim.
s_archon_rod: A succession of small measuring marks runs down the polished walnut shaft. Dealers attribute the rod to Megalon, although none can explain why so many scholars claim to have inherited it.
s_phex_whisper: The silver pommel bears a fox so discreetly engraved that it disappears beneath the thumb. A Horasian count is said to have offered a reward for the blade, and a larger one for the thief's name.
s_tusk: The pale head follows the curve of an enormous tusk, its cutting edge reinforced with steel. Albernian storytellers insist the beast swallowed a village; the hunters tend to stop at saying it was large.
s_thunderbolt: A finely fitted ratchet draws back the heavy steel bow. The maker's copper lightning mark is less a boast than a warning to keep one's fingers clear of the mechanism.
s_widowmaker: Black leather protects the long ricasso, polished smooth by a succession of mailed hands. No noble crest adorns the blade; those who carried it were paid for their work, not remembered for their lineage.
s_sentinel_mail: Blue-grey edging has been carefully renewed around the old iron rings. The clasp bears the castle's device, and a name worn too faint to read. Local tales say its last sentinel never abandoned his post.
s_thinking_cap: Gold stars have been sewn onto the faded blue cloth with surprising care. Scholars disagree about the constellation they form, sometimes changing their minds between one reading and the next.
s_dancer_boots: Soft leather and supple soles conceal more careful work than their lightness suggests. An elven maker has stitched a winding path around each ankle, leaving neither path with an obvious end.
s_forgefather_gauntlets: The squared knuckle plates resemble the faces of little anvils. Old scorch marks remain beneath the copper cuffs, where a previous owner has scratched a private prayer to Angrosch.
s_salamander_scale: Dark reddish scales have been riveted over a lining of dwarven mail. The smith left a small salamander on the clasp, perhaps to honour the creature whose hide made such difficult work worthwhile.
s_second_wind: A cloudy stone sits low in a band carved with curling winds. Hold it to the light and the pale shape within seems to turn, like weather gathering beyond a distant ridge.
s_unshaken_mind: A warding figure hangs within clear amber, untouched by the little flaws around it. The frame is plain and sturdy: whoever made this amulet valued a settled mind above outward splendour.
s_falcon_eye: A yellow topaz is held between two engraved falcons. The stone catches even a narrow shaft of light, recalling the patient attention of a bird watching the ground far below.
s_angrosch_wall: The raised spine of this shield divides a mountain device above a small anvil. Hammer marks remain visible beneath the finish; its maker saw no reason to hide honest work.
s_lucky_star: An irregular pale stone rests in a setting too carefully made for an ordinary trinket. A gambler claimed it fell into his cup during a losing throw. He never explained whether the throw improved.
l_fang_lioness: Ivory, red leather and a fine lightning inlay mark this saber as the work of an accomplished armourer. Amazon tradition links it to an early queen of Kurkum; the many repairs suggest a relic carried into battle rather than kept above an altar.
l_angrosch_hammer: The striking face is plain, its polish earned through use rather than decoration. Among the forge-clans, this hammer is said to preserve a spark of Angrosch's first fire. Even cautious smiths handle it with respect.
l_sala_mandra: Pale wood and dark horn meet beneath delicate silver work. An old elven song places a bow like this in the hands of a singer of Sala Mandra, though songs seldom pause to describe a weapon closely enough to settle an argument.
l_eye_hesinde: A cloudy crystal lens rests within a bronze serpent at the head of this staff. Fine threads of light seem to cross inside the glass when magic is worked nearby, inviting study rather than offering easy answers.
l_phex_laugh: A pale tooth has been fitted with a narrow steel edge and a silver guard. Its owner claimed it had been stolen from Japhgur twice. Asked how it came to be returned the first time, he merely smiled.
l_wyrmbane: The long blade carries an old repair near the guard, joined with extraordinary care. A tale from Gratenfels credits it with a lindwurm's death; the sword itself offers only scars and a stubborn resistance to heat.
l_kurkum_aegis: An ivory lioness strides across the worn red facing, above a silver lightning stroke. The device has been repainted over older damage. Its keepers remember the shield's bearers by name, and its armourers with equal gratitude.
l_umbracor_shard: A dark red splinter is held in a cage of worked gold. Those who named it believed its slow inner light came from Umbracor himself. Whether relic or extraordinary stone, it has outlasted every explanation offered for it.
l_forgefather_plate: Broad plates and carefully fitted joints give this armour the dignity of a royal commission. Murolosh tradition associates its pattern with an ancient king, while the leather beneath bears the repairs of more recent generations.
l_seven_gazes: Seven eyes are worked into the robe's gold embroidery, each looking in a slightly different direction. By lamplight, it is difficult to decide whether the changing expression belongs to the stitching or to one's own tired eyes.
